problem: "Tap the bulb" is bad practice: tapping a glass thermometer can break the mercury/alcohol column or give a false reading, and it is not what settling at equilibrium requires.
fix: Wait without touching the bulb, then confirm that two successive readings agree before recording the value.

problem: An adiabatic wall alone does not define an isolated system; an isolated system also exchanges no work and no mass with the surroundings. A wall that only blocks heat gives a thermally insulated system.
fix: Adiabatic wall: no heat transfer. A system enclosed by such a wall, with no work and no mass crossing the boundary, is an isolated system.
